newsitem.title: UK: Russian fuel oil exports tripled in February.
newsitem.headline: Russian fuel oil exports tripled in February.

text.p: Russian exports of heavy fuel oil from the Baltics and the Black Sea rose by around five percent in February on a monthly basis to nearly one million tonnes, traders and industry analysts said.

But exports were between two and three times higher than last year, and traders said this has been a key factor in falling prices which have seen the value of fuel oil fall against Brent crude oil by around $20 a tonne since last year.

Total fuel oil exports from both the Baltics and the Black Sea were some 975,000 tonnes in February compared to around 930,000 tonnes in January, consultants Petro Logistics estimated in weekly reports based on tanker movements.

Fuel oil traders estimated that of this, around 600,000 tonnes of February's total exports emerged from the Baltic ports of Klaipeda, Ventspils, St Petersburg and Tallinn, while some 400,000 tonnes were exported from the Black Sea ports of Odessa, Novorossiisk, Tuapse and Batumi.
Dealers attribute the dramatic year-on-year rise largely to the Russian government's failure this year to repeat the export ban that had been imposed in previous winters.
They also cited increasing sophistication on the part of Russian traders who are keen to sell less during the summer months, when prices are traditionally depressed, and export more in winter.

While exact export totals for each port were not available, shipping inspectors Petrak said exports in February from the Black Sea ports of Odessa, Tuapse and Novorossiisk were 105,000, 120,000 and 105,000 tonnes respectively, while exports from the Baltic port of Ventspils were 270,000 tonnes.

Traders said that the falling value of fuel oil against crude was mostly because of flagging long term demand - as Europe's power generators increasingly consume more natural gas and move away from the relatively more expensive and polluting fuel oil.

This pattern has been most noticeable in Italy, Europe's largest buyer of fuel oil, where official statistics showed that fuel oil consumption by power generators fell in January by 33 percent year-on-year.
Italian industry sources have said that they think consumption of natural gas in their country will grow at an average of around 10 percent per year from now until the year 2000.
In Britain, latest data from the government's Department of Trade and Industry showed that consumption of gas outpaced that of oil for the first time in 1996.
